title: The two jobs of y at the end of a word
examples: Why does y say ee in happy?
What sound does y make in my?

figure.name: x-word
figure.note: Here y says the ee in tree.

explain.say: Did you know y can do a vowel job? At the end of a word, y has two jobs. Look at happy on the board. Let us find out what y is doing here.

draw.text: The two jobs of y at the end of a word

draw.name: x-word
draw.note: Here y says the ee in tree.

explain.say: Look at the part glowing: two p letters. Together they make just one sound, the first sound in pig. Two letters, one sound. Tap it once.

draw.name: x-word
draw.note: Here y says the ee in tree.

explain.say: Now the y at the end glows. In happy, y makes the sound in tree. Happy, sunny, funny. Can you say happy with a big smile?

draw.name: x-word
draw.note: Here y says the ee in tree.

explain.say: Now look at my. It is a short word. Here y says the name of the letter i, like in fly and sky. Point to yourself and say my!
Here is a handy tip on the board. One beat, like my, and y usually says i. Two beats or more, like happy, and y usually says ee. Brilliant! Where would you put the word try?

faq.q: Why does y sometimes say ee?
faq.a: At the end of a word with two or more beats, like happy and baby, y usually makes the sound in tree.

faq.q: When does y say the name of i?
faq.a: In short words with one beat, like my, fly and sky, y usually says the name of the letter i.
asks: Why does y say i in my?

faq.a: y can be both. At the start of a word, like yes, it is a consonant. At the end, like in my or happy, it does a vowel job.

faq.q: Why are there two p letters in happy?
faq.a: The two p letters make just one sound. They help keep the a short, so we say hap and not hape.

faq.q: How do I choose which sound y makes?
faq.a: Clap the word. One clap, like fly, and y usually says i. Two or more claps, like hap-py, and y usually says ee.
asks: How do I know what y says?

facts: At the end of one-beat words like my and sky, y usually sounds like the name of the letter i.
At the end of longer words like happy and baby, y usually sounds like the ee in tree.

quiz.why: Pup-py has two beats, so y says ee.
